Logical Equivalences, Homomorphism Indistinguishability, and Forbidden Minors

      Abstract

      Two graphs GGG and HHH are homomorphism indistinguishable over a class of graphs F\mathcal{F}F if hom⁡(F,G)=hom⁡(F,H)\hom(F, G) = \hom(F, H)hom(F,G)=hom(F,H) for every F∈FF \in \mathcal{F}F∈F. Many equivalence relations comparing graphs such as (quantum) isomorphism, spectral equivalences, equivalences with respect to counting logic fragments can be characterised as homomorphism indistinguishability relations over natural graph classes.

      This submission formalises the correspondence between closure properties of a graph class F\mathcal{F}F and preservation properties of its homomorphism indistinguishability relation ≡F\equiv_{\mathcal{F}}≡F​. Its main results are that ≡F\equiv_{\mathcal{F}}≡F​ is preserved under taking complements if and only if cl(F)\mathrm{cl}(\mathcal{F})cl(F) is minor-closed. Both rest on a lemma of Curticapean, Dell and Marx turning a linear combination of homomorphism counts determined by ≡F\equiv_{\mathcal{F}}≡F​ into membership in cl(F)\mathrm{cl}(\mathcal{F})cl(F), which in turn rests on Lovász's theorem that homomorphism counts determine a finite graph up to isomorphism.

      The submission also formalises Roberson's conjecture (minor-closed union-closed graph classes are homomorphism distinguishing closed) and many basic notions from homomorphism indistinguishability including Lovász's theorem (homomorphism indistinguishability over all graphs is isomorphism) and the invertibility of the matrix (hom⁡(F,G))F,G(\hom(F, G))_{F, G}(hom(F,G))F,G​.
